title: [finding] the pm-dispatch `Part of` instruction should warn about the sentence that names who will close the card — measured red-then-green on PR #12777
body:
Filed unassigned and **ungraded** by the `domain:services` PM seat, session `session_0194kbQJxUvv2yvsGRtuXpP5`. ⛔ Not graded, not routed. ⚠️ Touches `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md`, a **governed surface** — filed as a card rather than edited, and the maintainer's merge is the review record.

## The near-miss, and it is measured rather than argued

On PR #12777 the PM ruled the closing keyword down from `Fixes #11833` to `Part of #11833`, because #11833 carries `has_children: true` with `sub_issues_summary {total: 1, completed: 0}` — `Fixes` would have auto-retired a parent showing 0 of 1 children complete, as a merge side effect rather than anyone's decision.

While making that edit, the dev's own **explanatory prose** contained:

> The PM will **close #11833** deliberately after the merge.

GitHub's reference parser matches `close` / `fixes` / `resolves` plus a number **regardless of the surrounding sentence**. That bookkeeping line would have re-armed the exact auto-close the edit existed to prevent.

⭐ **This is not a hypothetical the dev reported — the gate caught it red.** Two runs of the repo's own check on the same PR, same head:

| run | time | conclusion |
|---|---|---|
| `98634479836` — *Part-of PR must not also close its card* | 2026-08-27 18:52:17Z | ❌ **failure** |
| `98634968551` — same check, after the rephrase | 2026-08-27 18:54:28Z | ✅ success |

The dev caught it on read-back, rephrased, and the gate went green. ⇒ The control worked exactly as designed; this card is about the **instruction**, not the gate.

## Why the instruction is worth changing anyway

The negation trap is already documented for prose like *"this does not fix #N"*. ⚠️ The higher-risk shape is the one that bit here and is **not** covered: the sentence naming **who will retire the card and when**. It reads as pure bookkeeping, it is written *because* the author is being careful about not closing, and it is therefore most likely to appear in exactly the PR bodies switching to `Part of`.

⇒ The body most likely to write a closing keyword next to the card number is the body **explaining why it is not closing that card**. The warning belongs where the lane tells a dev to switch to `Part of`, not only where closing keywords are discussed.

⛔ **No wording proposed here**, and no recommendation on whether it earns a governed-surface edit at all — the gate already catches it, at the cost of one red CI round. Whether that cost is worth a doc change is a grading call, and the file is maintainer-authored.

## Provenance

Raised by the dev on #11833 as an open question (option A: leave it per-PR; option B: promote it), with its own recommendation of **B, weakly**, and the honest note that *"nothing is blocked either way"*. The PM agrees with B and is recording it here rather than acting on it, because `.claude/**` is not this seat's to edit.

## Dedup

**#12668** (`pm:queue`, `domain:skills`) is the nearest neighbour — *"pm-dispatch decision framework: add three maintainer-ruled standing rules"*. Different content (pull-directed priority order, startup-stage no-gradualism, release-reminder discipline), but it touches the same file, so ⭐ **if this is graded worth doing, folding it into that card is likely cheaper than a second governed-surface PR.** That is a routing suggestion, not a claim about priority.

## Re-check

```
gh api repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/check-runs/98634479836 --jq .conclusion   # failure
gh api repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/check-runs/98634968551 --jq .conclusion   # success
```
